subject: SCIENCE
title: Living or Nonliving?
objective: Use multiple characteristics as evidence when discussing living things.
introduction: A seed may rest before it sprouts, while a toy car moves only when pushed. What evidence helps Maxine tell living from non-living?

vocabulary.definition: The ability to make things happen or to do work, such as growing or moving.
The pattern of being born, growing, changing, and producing new living things.
A living thing that grows in soil and makes food.

activities.instruction: Watch Milo use several signs to tell living from non-living.
activities.content: Living organisms use energy, maintain internal processes, grow or develop, respond, and belong to reproducing life cycles; one visible sign alone is not enough.

feedback.retry: Check several signs—growth, energy use, response, and a life cycle—not movement alone.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: Text alternative: Living organisms use energy, maintain internal processes, grow or develop, respond, and belong to reproducing life cycles; one visible sign alone is not enough.

activities.accessibilityAlternative: A numbered list of the same examples is available for keyboard and screen-reader use.

items.prompt: Milo compares a sprouting seed, a plant, and a toy car. Which statement about living things is true?

options.text: Every individual must visibly reproduce
Living things use energy, grow, respond to surroundings, and belong to life cycles; one sign alone is not enough.
Movement alone proves life
Anything that changes color is alive

items.explanation: Living things show several signs, such as growth, energy use, response, and a life cycle. A toy car can move, and one visible sign alone does not prove life.

items.prompt: A seed rests in soil for weeks before sprouting. Which statement is correct?

options.text: Fire is a living organism
A moving toy car is alive
A seed can be dormant and living
Anything that moves is alive

items.explanation: A seed can be dormant—resting while still alive—and later sprout. Fire and toy cars can move, but they are not living organisms.

items.prompt: Milo writes four claims about living things. Which statement is NOT true?

options.text: A seed can be dormant and living
Fire moves but is not an organism
Movement alone proves life
A plant grows and uses energy

items.explanation: Movement alone does not prove life: fire and cars move without being organisms. A seed can rest while alive, and a plant grows and uses energy.

items.prompt: Maxine pushes a toy car and sees it move. Which statement helps her decide whether movement means life?

options.text: Dormant seeds are always dead.
Everything that moves is alive.
Movement alone does not prove something is living.
A moving object always grows.

items.explanation: Cars and fire can move without living. To identify life, check several signs such as growth, energy use, response, and a life cycle.

items.prompt: A classroom plant grows toward a window and uses water. Which statement is true?

options.text: A plant grows and uses energy
Dormancy means non-living
Movement alone proves life
A plant is alive only when it has flowers

items.explanation: Growth and energy use are evidence that the plant is living. A dormant seed can still be alive, and flowers or movement alone are not the whole test.
